questions.question: Explain two reasons why Elizabethans explored the New World. (4 marks)

points.text: Two reasons: (1) Trade - English merchants wanted direct access to Asian luxury goods (spices, silk) without paying Italian or Ottoman middlemen, and the potential profits were enormous; (2) Rivalry with Spain - Spain and Portugal had a monopoly on New World trade through the Treaty of Tordesillas, and England wanted to challenge this by establishing its own colonies and trade routes. questions.question: Describe Drake's circumnavigation of the world (1577-80). (4 marks)

questions.question: Why did the Roanoke colony fail? (8 marks)

points.text: The Roanoke colony failed because: it was poorly provisioned and lacked adequate supplies; the war with Spain diverted ships and delayed resupply missions; the settlers antagonised the local Native Americans by demanding food and burning villages; the location on Roanoke Island was swampy and unsuitable; the settlers lacked survival skills for the new environment; Raleigh never visited the colony

questions.question: How did English exploration affect indigenous peoples in the Americas? (4 marks)

points.text: English exploration affected indigenous peoples negatively: European diseases (smallpox, influenza) killed large numbers; English settlers attacked villages when Native Americans refused to provide food (e.g. Grenville burning Aquascogoc in 1585); land was taken without consent; some Native Americans were captured and taken to England; missionaries attempted to destroy traditional beliefs. questions.question: Explain what happened to the "Lost Colony" of Roanoke. (4 marks)

points.text: The "Lost Colony" of Roanoke was the third group of settlers sent by Raleigh in 1587, comprising approximately 115 people. John White, the governor, returned to England for supplies in late 1587 but was delayed by the Spanish Armada. When he returned in August 1590, the settlement was completely deserted.
